items.headline: US 20-yr auction (Oct 21): $13B at 5.469% — record high since the May-2020 reintroduction; tailed WI 5.460% by 0.9bp (4th tail in a row, improved on Sept's 2bp); B/C 2.73 (vs 2.57 Sept); directs record 31.6%; indirects 58.2% (avg 65.2% — soft foreign demand). Dow Jones/WSJ: 'softer-than-expected'; Barron's: little market reaction, yields barely budged
items.source: Dow Jones Newswires via Morningstar/WSJ; InvestingLive

items.headline: NY close: DXY ~101.7 flat near the 3-week low; EUR/USD 1.1233 flat; GBP/USD 1.3395 (+0.11%) on hot UK CPI; USD/JPY ~158.1 flat; AUD/USD 0.7032 (+0.2-0.3%, 3-week high) — the day's best G10 performer on RBA repricing; USD/CAD 1.4058 flat; NZD/USD 0.5701 into tonight's CPI

Brent settled $108.82 (+0.03%) — snaps a 2-session losing streak after running ~$110.4 overnight and fading on debunked mediation headlines; WTI Dec settled $97.15 (-0.68%, second straight down day, -6.28% over two sessions) on US SPR/heating-oil reserve loan news; EIA -3.1M draw partly offset by +1.7M distillate build
items.source: Dow Jones Data Talk via Morningstar

items.headline: Bailey fireside (8am CT): zero major-wire carry of new rate-policy remarks (headline-only: would not discuss monetary policy) — below bar, actual stays null

RBA Nov-3 hike ~42% (LSEG, Oct 21; OIS 41-55%): Goldman Sachs flipped to a November call (25bp to 4.85%, 'the fifth of 2026'); Hauser's 'materially worse' inflation outlook the trigger; Q3 CPI Oct 28 the pivot

BoJ Dec hike ~80% (Japan Times/Bloomberg, Oct 21, via ex-BoJ exec Maeda who expects Dec then Mar/Apr) — up from ~73-74%; Oct 29-30 a hold at ~88-90% (OIS); Reuters: BoJ may upgrade inflation forecast while holding

ECB Dec hike ~76% (ECB Watch, ~Oct 15 vintage; prior ~88% read stale); Commerzbank: one Dec hike + slightly more by mid-2027. Eurozone natural gas broke EUR 90/MWh (first since Dec 2022); OAT 4.948% (+2.9bp), Bund 3.414% (+1.8bp) — spread ~153bp (WSJ/Tradeweb)
Gold ~$4,118 (-0.2%, 5th straight down day) — trading December-hike odds (~90%), not oil headlines; mid-session re-tested $4,150; Dec futures $4,136.20

UK Sep CPI verified: 3.5% y/y beat (vs 3.4% fcst; highest since Oct 2025 on energy; core 2.8% in line; services 3.7% sticky; PPI +4.6% vs 4.3%) — GBP/USD +0.1% to 1.339, EUR/GBP 83.80p strongest in 17 months; Nov-5 BoE ~96-98%, no repricing
BoC Oct-28 hike ~90-95%: CORRA OIS 95% (BlueGamma, Oct 21); LSEG ~85% (Oct 20); Spectra 83.9% — firmed toward a near-done deal from ~30% Friday

France 10Y OAT hits 5.00% (first since Jul 2002); OAT-Bund ~157-160bp Wednesday (widest since the 2009-11 crisis); revenue-section first reading postponed to Oct 27; FinMin Lescure floated Article 49.3; Moody's reviews France Friday (Aa3 neg)

Houthis DENY launching drones toward Medina today; Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted drones over Medina and the Eastern region — contradictory wire-level claims; Shabwa camp toll 73 (Reuters, Oct 21)

PBoC first overnight reverse repo: sold ¥80bn overnight (zero 7-day; ¥56bn 7-day matured) — net inject ¥24bn; yuan midpoint 6.7192 (strongest since Feb 2023); Commerzbank: operational tweak, no FX impact
NZ Q3 CPI tonight 4:45pm CT (0.8% q/q, 3.8% y/y fc; RBNZ proj 3.9%) — the Oct-28 RBNZ decider; hike ~80-81% to 3.00%, December second hike ~50%
France to deploy military for weekend protests; curfews 'where required' — EUR/USD pinned ~1.1220 on fiscal unrest
Houthis claim attacks on Aramco Yanbu, Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh/Abha airports — unverified by Reuters; Saudi silent
Japan September trade deficit -¥536.6bn vs -¥181bn forecast; exports +16.7% y/y miss (+20.1% exp); mineral-fuel imports +39.4%
GBP/USD +0.66% to 1.339 intraday as UK jobs beat (unemp 4.7% vs 4.9%) locks in Nov 5 BoE hike; DXY -0.27% to 101.69
US pending home sales -7.3% m/m in September (vs -0.4% fcst); index 66.0 = record low since 2001
GDT Event 414: WMP +4.4% ($3,760/t), SMP +3.4% ($3,975/t) — powder-led firm read
US housing starts 1.221M SAAR miss (vs 1.30M fcst, -7.4% y/y); permits 1.400M in line; 30-yr mortgage 7.40%
German producer prices rise 6.7% y/y in September, beating 6.2% consensus
